statement.p: Find the first four terms of the Taylor series for the function \cos(x) about the point a = \pi/4. (Your answers should include the variable x when appropriate.)

static.solution:
\cos(x) and its first three derivatives are
f(x) = \cos(x), f'(x) = - \sin(x), f''(x) = - \cos(x), and f'''(x) = \sin(x). Thus, evaluating these at x = \pi/4, we get the terms
term 0 = {1\over\sqrt2}
term 1 = -{1\over\sqrt2}(x - {\pi\over 4})
term 2 = -{1\over2\sqrt2}(x - {\pi\over4})^2, and
term 3 = {{1\over6\sqrt2}}(x - {\pi\over4})^3.
Thus the series is \cos(x) = {1\over\sqrt2} - {1\over\sqrt2}(x - {\pi\over 4}) - {1\over2\sqrt2}(x - {\pi\over4})^2 + {{1\over6\sqrt2}}(x - {\pi\over4})^3 + \cdots.
